links.outcome: Trauma surgeon triage accuracy before vs after LLM exposure, compared with standalone LLM accuracy
links.effect: Human accuracy rose from 73.7% to 75.8% after LLM exposure (p = 0.04, Bonferroni p = 0.12); odds ratio 2.57 (95% CI 1.39 to 6.83). Standalone LLM accuracy was 83.5% vs 78.9% for humans.
links.quote: In prospective evaluation, human triage accuracy improved after LLM exposure (73.7% [69.8 to 77.2]) to 75.8% ([71.9 to 79.2], p = 0.04, Bonferroni p = 0.12), significantly improving the odds of a correct triage decision (odds ratio 2.57, 95% CI 1.39 to 6.83, p < 0.01).

unlisted_practices: Structured 'Essential Transcripts' via named entity recognition to shorten inputs while preserving triage accuracy
Entity ablation testing of which triage parameters drive LLM accuracy

screen.reason: The study empirically tests whether providing LLM-generated triage recommendations to trauma surgeons (human-in-the-loop AI assistance) improves clinician triage decisions compared to unassisted decisions.

primary.practice: AI-assisted clinical decision making (pre- vs post-LLM clinician triage)
